facts.fact_text: Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan.
Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the 19 February 2008 election process.
Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan announced that the 19 February 2008 presidential election had not been free and fair.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies from 20 February 2008 onwards was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
Several hundred demonstrators stayed at Freedom Square around the clock, having set up a camp.
At the material time, the applicant was an opposition member of parliament.
At the material time, the applicant was a supporter of Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan.
The applicant regularly attended the ongoing demonstrations at Freedom Square from 20 February 2008 onwards.
The applicant occasionally gave speeches at the ongoing demonstrations at Freedom Square from 20 February 2008 onwards.
On 1 March 2008, at approximately 6-7 a.m., a police operation was conducted at Freedom Square in Yerevan where several hundred demonstrators were camping.
The applicant alleged that the police had violently attacked the demonstrators at Freedom Square with rubber batons during the 1 March 2008 police operation.
The applicant alleged that the police had violently attacked the demonstrators at Freedom Square with electric shock devices during the 1 March 2008 police operation.
The applicant alleged that the police terminated the assembly at Freedom Square during the 1 March 2008 police operation.
As a result of the 1 March 2008 police operation at Freedom Square, clashes took place between the police and the demonstrators.
On 1 March 2008 a criminal case was instituted under several Articles of the Armenian Criminal Code in connection with the events at Freedom Square.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of organising and holding an unlawful assembly.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of incitement to disobedience of police orders to terminate the unlawful assembly.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of illegal possession of arms and ammunition.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of life-threatening assaults on police officers.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that, after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 presidential election, Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan, members of parliament K.S. and S.M., and the chief editor of Haykakan Zhamanak daily newspaper N.P., and others organised and held mass public events at Yerevan's Freedom Square in violation of the procedure prescribed by law.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan, members of parliament K.S. and S.M., the chief editor of Haykakan Zhamanak daily newspaper N.P., and others made calls inciting disobedience of decisions ordering an end to the events held in violation of the procedure prescribed by law.
The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that a number of participants in the mass events illegally possessed and carried illegally obtained arms and ammunition.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that on 1 March 2008 at around 6 a.m., when the police took measures to forcibly end the public events held in violation of the procedure prescribed by law in compliance with section 14 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the organisers and participants disobeyed the lawful orders of the police officers.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that the organisers and participants committed a life- and health-threatening assault on police officers with clubs, metal rods and other adapted objects, causing the police officers injuries of varied severity.

The Government alleged that the disorder which took place in Yerevan on 1 and 2 March 2008 had been incited and organised by the applicant in conspiracy with several other active opposition supporters.

The applicant disputed the Government's allegation that the disorder which took place in Yerevan on 1 and 2 March 2008 had been incited and organised by him in conspiracy with several other active opposition supporters.

On 2 March 2008 another criminal case was instituted under, inter alia, Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code (organising mass disorder involving murder) in connection with the events of 1 and 2 March 2008.

The decision to institute the criminal case on 2 March 2008 stated that Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan, members of parliament K.S. and S.M., the chief editor of Haykakan Zhamanak daily newspaper N.P., and others, not willing to concede defeat at the 19 February 2008 presidential election, with the aim of casting doubt on the election and discrediting the election and the authorities, from 1 March 2008 in the area of the Yerevan Mayor's Office and central streets organised mass disorder involving murders, violence, massacre, arson, destruction of property and armed resistance to public officials, with the use of firearms, explosives and other adapted objects.
On 4 March 2008 the General Prosecutor applied to the Armenian parliament with a request to have the applicant's parliamentary immunity lifted.
On 4 March 2008 the General Prosecutor applied to the Armenian parliament for authorisation to bring charges against the applicant.
On 4 March 2008 the General Prosecutor applied to the Armenian parliament for authorisation to have the applicant detained.
On 4 March 2008 the General Prosecutor applied to the Armenian parliament for authorisation to have three other members of parliament detained alongside the applicant.
The General Prosecutor's request of 4 March 2008 described the events which had taken place in Yerevan between 20 February and the early morning of 2 March 2008.

The General Prosecutor's request of 4 March 2008 stated that the evidence obtained in the case provided sufficient grounds to believe that the applicant and three other members of parliament had taken an active part in inciting violence with public calls they had made.

The General Prosecutor's request of 4 March 2008 stated that the evidence obtained in the case provided sufficient grounds to believe that the applicant and three other members of parliament had organised mass disorder through direct participation, instigation and various types of support, including the recruitment and arming of attackers.

The General Prosecutor's request of 4 March 2008 stated that there were sufficient grounds to bring charges against the applicant and three other members of parliament under Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code for organising mass disorder which had taken place in Yerevan between 20 February and 2 March 2008.

The General Prosecutor's request of 4 March 2008 stated that there were sufficient grounds to bring charges against the applicant and three other members of parliament under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (usurpation of State power) for organising mass disorder with the aim of a violent usurpation of State power in breach of the Constitution.
The General Prosecutor's request of 4 March 2008 stated that there was sufficient evidence justifying the applicant's detention, including the risk of absconding and obstructing justice.
On 4 March 2008 the Armenian parliament adopted a resolution granting the General Prosecutor's request to lift the applicant's parliamentary immunity and authorise charges and detention.
On 5 March 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.
On 5 March 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.

The charging decision of 5 March 2008 stated that after the opposition candidate lost at the 19 February 2008 presidential election, the applicant joined the opposition candidate's group of supporters and, having conspired with them to usurp State power in violation of the constitutional order, actively participated in carrying out activities for that purpose.

The charging decision of 5 March 2008 stated that the applicant's activities included discrediting the pre-election process and the conduct of the election, raising doubts among the international community regarding the legality of the election, instilling distrust towards the results among large segments of the population, creating illusions of public discontent and revolt, and organising and holding unlawful demonstrations aimed at destabilising the internal political situation.

The charging decision of 5 March 2008 stated that the applicant, three other members of parliament and a number of other opposition supporters incited and organised mass disorder which took place in Yerevan on 1 and 2 March 2008 and involved mass violence, massacre, arson, destruction and damage of public and private property, armed resistance to public officials and murder.
On 12 March 2008 the applicant was arrested by officers of the National Security Service of Armenia.
On 12 March 2008 the applicant was placed in detention on the basis of a court order.
The applicant's detention order was extended throughout the investigation and the trial.
On 13 March 2008 the applicant was questioned by the investigator.
On 13 March 2008 the applicant denied the charges under Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 13 March 2008 the applicant denied the charges under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 13 March 2008 the applicant refused to testify.
On 13 March 2008 a search was conducted in several premises belonging to the applicant, including a restaurant.
During the search on 13 March 2008 of premises belonging to the applicant, various types of ammunition and explosives were found and seized at a restaurant belonging to the applicant.
On 12 June 2008 an additional charge was brought against the applicant under Article 235 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code for illegal possession of ammunition and explosives.

The additional charge under Article 235 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code brought against the applicant on 12 June 2008 was made with reference to the items seized during the search of the applicant's premises on 13 March 2008.
On 1 December 2008 the prosecutor approved the bill of indictment against the applicant and six other opposition leaders, commonly known as the 'Case of Seven'.
The applicant's criminal case had been disjoined from criminal case no. 62202608 before being transferred for trial.
On 1 December 2008 the applicant's criminal case (the 'Case of Seven') was transferred for trial.
On 31 March 2009 the prosecutor replaced the charge against the applicant under Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code with a charge under Article 225 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 31 March 2009 the prosecutor dropped the charge against the applicant under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
The prosecutor dropped the charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code on the ground that, on 24 March 2009, Article 300 § 1 had been amended and could not be applied retroactively.
The prosecutor replaced the charge under Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code with a charge under Article 225 § 1 on the ground that, on 24 March 2009, Article 225 § 3 had been repealed.
On 1 April 2009 the case against the applicant was disjoined into separate proceedings.

During the trial, the Kotayk Regional Court called and heard at least thirteen prosecution witnesses, mostly demonstrators who had attended the assembly at Freedom Square, many from the applicant's region.
Five of the prosecution witnesses heard by the Kotayk Regional Court either fully or partially retracted the statements they had given against the applicant during the investigation.

The five prosecution witnesses who retracted their statements claimed that they had been either guided or dictated by the investigator, or that their statements had been extracted by ill-treatment or intimidation.
Two prosecution witnesses, T.K. and V.S., failed to appear before the Kotayk Regional Court.
The testimony of prosecution witness G.A. was interrupted at one of the hearings before the Kotayk Regional Court and never resumed.
The Kotayk Regional Court failed to secure the appearance of prosecution witnesses T.K. and V.S.
The Kotayk Regional Court decided to read out the pre-trial statements of prosecution witnesses T.K. and V.S. despite the applicant's objections.
Prosecution witness G.A. submitted that he had been intimidated by the applicant's relatives and did not wish to continue his testimony in court out of fear for his life.
The Kotayk Regional Court at first tried unsuccessfully to secure prosecution witness G.A.'s appearance before the court.
The Kotayk Regional Court decided to relieve prosecution witness G.A. from the obligation to appear and to rely on his pre-trial statement.

The applicant requested that the Head of the Special Investigative Service be summoned as a witness and examined in court in connection with the charge of illegal possession of ammunition and explosives.
The Kotayk Regional Court rejected the applicant's request to summon the Head of the Special Investigative Service as a witness.
On 22 June 2009 the Kotayk Regional Court found the applicant guilty under Article 225 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 22 June 2009 the Kotayk Regional Court found the applicant guilty under Article 235 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 22 June 2009 the Kotayk Regional Court sentenced the applicant to a total of eight years in prison.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that after the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 election were made public, the applicant, together with a group of people, starting from 20 February 2008 carried out organisational activities for the purpose of creating discontent in society and preparing the crowd gathered at Freedom Square for use of violence and disobedience.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant and his group bought household items and food for demonstrators and provided money to ensure the continuous presence of groups of people at the events at Freedom Square.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant and his group distributed rods, clubs, armature, Molotov cocktails, metal structures considered projectile cold weapons, firearms and ammunition to some of those taking part in the demonstrations at Freedom Square.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant, using his army commander's experience and his standing acquired during the fight for liberation of Artsakh and his influence among veterans of the Nagorno Karabakh war, declared during the demonstrations at Freedom Square that he would struggle until the end and demanded that demonstrators be ready to take decisive steps.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant incited those recruited in the town of Hrazdan and adjacent villages to participate in the demonstrations held in violation of the law, acting as their personal commander and leader.
The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant regularly circulated at Freedom Square accompanied by bodyguards and companions-in-arms as a show of strength to arouse the crowd.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that between 27 and 29 February 2008 the applicant organised the transportation of wooden and metal clubs, armature and Molotov cocktails to Freedom Square, where they were hidden in tents designated as 'Hrazdan', 'Kotchor' and 'Vanatur'.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that on 29 February 2008 operative information was received by the Armenian Police and the National Security Service that a group of persons intended to instigate mass disorder in Yerevan on 1 March 2008 through provocations and that a large quantity of clubs, metal rods, explosive substances, firearms and grenades were to be distributed among participants of the assembly at Freedom Square.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that in the early morning of 1 March 2008 the police tried to discover illegal items at Freedom Square and to prevent their use, and as a result of the police operation part of the objects brought for the purpose of carrying out mass disorder, including firearms and ammunition, were discovered at Freedom Square.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that thereafter participants of the assembly, led by the applicant's group, gathered in the area adjacent to the Myasnikyan monument, an important intersection of several streets of Yerevan situated in the vicinity of the French, Italian and Russian embassies.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that at around 11 a.m. on 1 March 2008 the participants of the mass disorder blocked Grigor Lusavorich street by placing trolleybuses along the carriageway and armed themselves with stones, rods, sticks, explosive substances, explosive devices, firearms and Molotov cocktails.
The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that Molotov cocktails were filled with flammable liquid immediately behind the platform at the Myasnikyan monument and in the nearby park.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant and others rejected the offer made by the authorities to hold the assembly in another location and, with their speeches and orders, gave instructions to the gathered crowd with the aim of keeping it there as long as possible.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that from 1 to 2 March 2008 mass disorder was perpetrated in the area of the Myasnikyan monument and the Yerevan Mayor's Office, as well as Grigor Lusavorich, Mashtots, Leo and Paronyan streets, with use of firearms, ammunition and explosive substances and devices, during which armed resistance was shown to the police and servicemen of the Police Troops.
The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that a total of 187 persons, including 32 civilians, sustained injuries as a result of the mass disorder of 1-2 March 2008.

The Kotayk Regional Court specified the number of persons injured and killed and vehicles damaged, as well as the pecuniary damage caused to the police, the city of Yerevan, the central district and private businesses as a result of the mass disorder of 1-2 March 2008.
The Kotayk Regional Court concluded that the mass disorder of 1-2 March 2008 had stopped only after the declaration of a state of emergency and its prevention by the actions of the police.

As regards the charge of illegal possession of ammunition and explosives, the Kotayk Regional Court found that the applicant had obtained the items in question at an unidentified time and illegally kept them in his restaurant's storage room.
In reaching its conclusions, the Kotayk Regional Court relied, inter alia, on the statements of the witnesses who had appeared in court and the pre-trial statements of witnesses T.K., V.S. and G.A.

As regards the pre-trial statements retracted in court, the Kotayk Regional Court found that the witnesses in question, as the applicant's companions-in-arms, friends and residents of his area, had retracted their statements because of being familiar and close with the applicant, and decided to give preference to their pre-trial statements.
On 22 July 2009 the applicant lodged an appeal against his conviction.
On 31 July 2009 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against his conviction.
On 31 July 2009 the Criminal Court of Appeal upheld the judgment of the Kotayk Regional Court.
On 30 August 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal on points of law.
On 10 September 2009 the Court of Cassation of Armenia declared the applicant's appeal on points of law inadmissible for lack of merit.

Five of the prosecution witnesses heard by the Kotayk Regional Court either fully or partially retracted the statements they had given against the applicant during the investigation.

The five prosecution witnesses who retracted their statements claimed that they had been either guided or dictated by the investigator, or that their statements had been extracted by ill-treatment or intimidation.
Two prosecution witnesses, T.K. and V.S., failed to appear before the Kotayk Regional Court.
The testimony of prosecution witness G.A. was interrupted at one of the hearings before the Kotayk Regional Court and never resumed.
The Kotayk Regional Court failed to secure the appearance of prosecution witnesses T.K. and V.S.
The Kotayk Regional Court decided to read out the pre-trial statements of prosecution witnesses T.K. and V.S. despite the applicant's objections.
Prosecution witness G.A. submitted that he had been intimidated by the applicant's relatives and did not wish to continue his testimony in court out of fear for his life.
The Kotayk Regional Court at first tried unsuccessfully to secure prosecution witness G.A.'s appearance before the court.
The Kotayk Regional Court decided to relieve prosecution witness G.A. from the obligation to appear and to rely on his pre-trial statement.

The applicant requested that the Head of the Special Investigative Service be summoned as a witness and examined in court in connection with the charge of illegal possession of ammunition and explosives.
The Kotayk Regional Court rejected the applicant's request to summon the Head of the Special Investigative Service as a witness.
On 22 June 2009 the Kotayk Regional Court found the applicant guilty under Article 225 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 22 June 2009 the Kotayk Regional Court found the applicant guilty under Article 235 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 22 June 2009 the Kotayk Regional Court sentenced the applicant to a total of eight years in prison.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that after the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 election were made public, the applicant, together with a group of people, starting from 20 February 2008 carried out organisational activities for the purpose of creating discontent in society and preparing the crowd gathered at Freedom Square for use of violence and disobedience.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant and his group bought household items and food for demonstrators and provided money to ensure the continuous presence of groups of people at the events at Freedom Square.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant and his group distributed rods, clubs, armature, Molotov cocktails, metal structures considered projectile cold weapons, firearms and ammunition to some of those taking part in the demonstrations at Freedom Square.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant, using his army commander's experience and his standing acquired during the fight for liberation of Artsakh and his influence among veterans of the Nagorno Karabakh war, declared during the demonstrations at Freedom Square that he would struggle until the end and demanded that demonstrators be ready to take decisive steps.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant incited those recruited in the town of Hrazdan and adjacent villages to participate in the demonstrations held in violation of the law, acting as their personal commander and leader.
The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant regularly circulated at Freedom Square accompanied by bodyguards and companions-in-arms as a show of strength to arouse the crowd.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that between 27 and 29 February 2008 the applicant organised the transportation of wooden and metal clubs, armature and Molotov cocktails to Freedom Square, where they were hidden in tents designated as 'Hrazdan', 'Kotchor' and 'Vanatur'.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that on 29 February 2008 operative information was received by the Armenian Police and the National Security Service that a group of persons intended to instigate mass disorder in Yerevan on 1 March 2008 through provocations and that a large quantity of clubs, metal rods, explosive substances, firearms and grenades were to be distributed among participants of the assembly at Freedom Square.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that in the early morning of 1 March 2008 the police tried to discover illegal items at Freedom Square and to prevent their use, and as a result of the police operation part of the objects brought for the purpose of carrying out mass disorder, including firearms and ammunition, were discovered at Freedom Square.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that thereafter participants of the assembly, led by the applicant's group, gathered in the area adjacent to the Myasnikyan monument, an important intersection of several streets of Yerevan situated in the vicinity of the French, Italian and Russian embassies.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that at around 11 a.m. on 1 March 2008 the participants of the mass disorder blocked Grigor Lusavorich street by placing trolleybuses along the carriageway and armed themselves with stones, rods, sticks, explosive substances, explosive devices, firearms and Molotov cocktails.
The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that Molotov cocktails were filled with flammable liquid immediately behind the platform at the Myasnikyan monument and in the nearby park.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that the applicant and others rejected the offer made by the authorities to hold the assembly in another location and, with their speeches and orders, gave instructions to the gathered crowd with the aim of keeping it there as long as possible.

The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that from 1 to 2 March 2008 mass disorder was perpetrated in the area of the Myasnikyan monument and the Yerevan Mayor's Office, as well as Grigor Lusavorich, Mashtots, Leo and Paronyan streets, with use of firearms, ammunition and explosive substances and devices, during which armed resistance was shown to the police and servicemen of the Police Troops.
The Kotayk Regional Court found it established that a total of 187 persons, including 32 civilians, sustained injuries as a result of the mass disorder of 1-2 March 2008.

The Kotayk Regional Court specified the number of persons injured and killed and vehicles damaged, as well as the pecuniary damage caused to the police, the city of Yerevan, the central district and private businesses as a result of the mass disorder of 1-2 March 2008.
The Kotayk Regional Court concluded that the mass disorder of 1-2 March 2008 had stopped only after the declaration of a state of emergency and its prevention by the actions of the police.

As regards the charge of illegal possession of ammunition and explosives, the Kotayk Regional Court found that the applicant had obtained the items in question at an unidentified time and illegally kept them in his restaurant's storage room.
In reaching its conclusions, the Kotayk Regional Court relied, inter alia, on the statements of the witnesses who had appeared in court and the pre-trial statements of witnesses T.K., V.S. and G.A.

As regards the pre-trial statements retracted in court, the Kotayk Regional Court found that the witnesses in question, as the applicant's companions-in-arms, friends and residents of his area, had retracted their statements because of being familiar and close with the applicant, and decided to give preference to their pre-trial statements.
On 22 July 2009 the applicant lodged an appeal against his conviction.
On 31 July 2009 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against his conviction.
On 31 July 2009 the Criminal Court of Appeal upheld the judgment of the Kotayk Regional Court.
On 30 August 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal on points of law.
On 10 September 2009 the Court of Cassation of Armenia declared the applicant's appeal on points of law inadmissible for lack of merit.
